vectors.description: A publisher preserves provider identity, source metadata, an exact bounded grant, access, rights, canonical actions, and a minimized receipt.
A society keeps a correction status, status route, correction warning, and responsible organization attached.
A library names the actual rights holder and supplies metadata plus an exact route rather than protected third-party content.
A provider error remains a valid privacy-minimized envelope without echoing a request.
A receipt cannot be detached from the provider that issued the response.
A library resource response cannot imply ownership by omitting the actual rights holder.
vectors.expectedDiagnostic: library resource responses must identify the actual rights holder

vectors.description: A useful resource must retain an exact open or deep-link action to its canonical provider context.
A client or provider cannot silently drop the warning attached to a corrected resource.
vectors.expectedDiagnostic: corrected resource must carry a correction warning

vectors.description: A withdrawn resource remains discoverable as metadata but cannot supply a retrieved content unit.
vectors.expectedDiagnostic: retrieval must not supply a retracted or withdrawn content unit

vectors.description: A supplied content unit cannot be detached from its resource metadata.
A receipt carrying query text violates the closed, privacy-minimized 0.1 receipt contract.

mutations.value: sensitive raw query must not survive
